thread:
oncall-bot: :pager: PROD ALERT — multiple NCCL communicator timeouts observed across ranks on prod-gpu-cluster. Affected service: driver/inference-runtime. Severity: P1. Please acknowledge and follow the runbook.
Alice M: acked. landing on this. Which nodes are showing timeouts?
SRE Infra: seeing errors reported on nodes gpu-node-17, gpu-node-18, gpu-node-21. Kernel messages show repeated NVLINK link down/up events + CUDA driver errors.
Ben R: I'm on call, jumping in. Any customer-facing impact yet?
Customer Success: one enterprise customer reported elevated error rates (40% inference failures) starting ~12:48 UTC. They said requests hang and then error out.
ML Runtime: quick note — jobs are using pipeline parallelism across 8 ranks, NCCL used for allreduce + allgather. If a single rank loses connectivity the whole model can hang.
Alice M: ok first priority: isolate affected pods. Ben, can you get kubectl logs for the failing pod on gpu-node-17 and paste recent NCCL/CUDA lines?
Ben R: running: 
```
kubectl -n prod logs inference-rt-7f9b -c runtime --tail=200
```
Ben R: logs snippet: 
```
I0312 12:47:59 NCCL INFO Comm 0x7f9a2f created
E0312 12:48:05 NCCL WARN Timeout waiting for operation
E0312 12:48:05 CUDA Error 700: Launch failed
```
Also see kernel: `nvidia: GPU power state change, GPU 0 link down` repeated.
SRE Infra: cross-checking node dmesg: 
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.568012] nvlink: nvlink0: link 1 flapping
```
ML Runtime: Xid 79 indicates a GPU crash / driver reset. That explains communicator errors. Could be driver bug or hardware fault.
Alice M: mitigation plan: (1) cordon gpu-node-17 and 18 to prevent new pods, (2) evict and restart affected inference pods (gracefully when possible), (3) migrate critical customer jobs to healthy nodes, (4) enable NCCL async error handling for runtime temporarily to fail fast and avoid hangs. Ben, run cordon now?
Ben R: doing cordon: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-17 gpu-node-18` — done. Draining one pod now: `kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` — eviction hung on one inference pod (stuck in terminating).
SRE Infra: terminating stuck pods likely due to container runtime waiting on GPU reclaim after driver reset. We'll force delete and restart kubelet on node.
Deploy Bot: starting rolling restart for inference service across non-cordoned nodes per playbook.
Ben R: forced delete executed: `kubectl delete pod inference-rt-7f9b --grace-period=0 --force` — pod terminated and scheduled to healthy node gpu-node-05. New pod reporting OK so far.
ML Runtime: change to runtime env: set `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1` and `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0` to reduce flaky NIC selection. Also reduce `BATCH_TOKENS` for in-flight work to reduce memory pressure during the incident.
Alice M: applied env bumps to staging tasks; rolling to prod with 3 replicas first. Observability: tracing shows tail latencies reduced as those pods restart.
SRE Infra: node-level: gpu-node-18 shows repeated ECC corrected errors and a single uncorrectable ECC — ops recommends isolating that board. We'll move workloads off and schedule hardware checks.
Customer Success: informing customer: "We're investigating GPU cluster errors causing intermittent inference failures; we've isolated affected nodes and are migrating workloads. We'll follow up with RCA and ETA."
Ben R: observed a second symptom: NCCL communicators failing earlier in create phase — logs show rank negotiation failure: `NCCL WARN NET/Connect` and `NCCL ERROR Unhandled System Error`. That points to cross-node network flaps too. SRE, are there any fabric events?
SRE Infra: checking fabric controller — IB fabric shows short route flaps between racks at 12:47:50-12:48:10. Looks like simultaneous NVLink/IB issues, could be coincidental or due to power disruption on the rack.
ML Runtime: for immediate mitigation we should enable per-pod fallback: use `--fallback-model=cpu` or lower-parallel config for customer-critical jobs to stop them from hanging. Also add aggressive timeouts so rpc calls fail fast instead of waiting for NCCL timeouts.
Alice M: agreed. Ben, can you patch critical deployment with lower parallelism and a fallback model? Do a canary rollout (1 pod) then scale.
Ben R: patch applied (canary 1/3). Canary started and passed healthchecks. Rolling to rest.
Deploy Bot: canary promoted after 2m of healthy metrics.
SRE Infra: node maintenance window scheduled for gpu-node-18 hardware swap. We'll coordinate with ML Runtime and CS on any SLA notes.
Alice M: short-term post-incident tasks: 1) mark nodes out of rotation, 2) update incident timeline, 3) notify customers with RCA within 24h. Long-term: add automated node health detection that triggers preemptive migration if NVLINK or Xid patterns appear.
Customer Success: prepared message for affected customers.
ML Runtime: follow-up actions from runtime team: add `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` for a short window to capture rendezvous flow, add rank-level watchdog to restart stuck ranks, and evaluate NCCL driver upgrade matrix.
Ben R: all responders, please ack when wrapped up.
Alice M: wrapping — incident moved to mitigation state at 12:52 UTC. Will create postmortem. :white_check_mark:
